article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Chicago closed Week 8 with a 34-17 win at Seattle, the board has not flipped to Week 9 yet, and Baltimore's quarterback for Thursday night is still not named.

items.headline: Lead: Chicago closes Week 8 with a 34-17 rout at Seattle
paragraphs: Week 8 is over. Chicago beat Seattle 34-17 on Monday night at Lumen Field, pulling away in the second half after leading 13-9 at halftime.

Caleb Williams went 24 of 34 for 247 yards and a touchdown. D'Andre Swift ran 27 times for 69 yards and scored three touchdowns, all in the second half. Seattle's Sam Darnold went 17 of 34 for 188 yards with two touchdowns and an interception, and was sacked three times.
Chicago moves to 6-2. Seattle, the defending champions, falls to 4-4. There is no game today, Tuesday — the next kickoff is Thursday night.
items.takeaway: Bears 34, Seahawks 17: Williams 247 yards, Swift three touchdowns, and Week 8 is closed.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Baltimore's quarterback for Thursday is still not named
paragraphs: Baltimore's quarterback room is still unsettled for Thursday night against Jacksonville. Lamar Jackson did not participate in Monday's walkthrough with the right thumb injury that requires surgery and a move to injured reserve. Tyler Huntley did not participate with his toe injury and is out for Thursday, with reports saying he is set to miss extended time.

That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who finished Sunday's loss at Buffalo, as the next man up. He was limited Monday with an ankle injury, but head coach Jesse Minter said he has a chance to play Thursday. Baltimore signed quarterback Austin Reed to the practice squad Monday as cover.

One more Baltimore note: kicker Tyler Loop did not participate with a groin injury, and Jake Moody is expected to kick Thursday. The starter decision is expected in the next day or two, and the inactive list lands about 90 minutes before kickoff. The app's board has not flipped to Week 9 yet, so do not look to it for Thursday's quarterback — watch the practice reports instead.
items.takeaway: Jackson to injured reserve, Huntley out Thursday, Fagnano limited with an ankle injury but with a chance to play — starter still to be named.

items.headline: No game today — next up is Thursday night in Baltimore
paragraphs: Tuesday is a blank day on the schedule. The next game is Jacksonville at Baltimore on Thursday, November 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET.
That is also the game with the one real unknown left this week: Baltimore's starting quarterback. Everything else about Thursday can wait for the board to flip and the practice reports to land.
items.takeaway: No game today; next kickoff is Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET, Jacksonville at Baltimore.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Monday's cards, settled: the favorite lost, the +3 won
paragraphs: Monday night settles the board's Week 8 cards, and it is a useful split. Hit Rate was the Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings. Seattle lost outright, so that pick lost. Hit Rate is the pick the app rates most likely to win — it is not a promise, and favorites lose too. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced and Value were both Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings. Chicago won outright, so that pick won. Two cards pointing at the same pick is not two separate bets; it is one pick the app likes two ways.
If you tracked Monday night, log both sides of that result. Settlement in the tracker is manual, and it only works if you are honest with yourself.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate Seattle moneyline -175 lost; Balanced and Value Chicago +3 -102 won — one pick, liked two ways, and a reminder that the likeliest pick still loses sometimes.

items.headline: The board has not flipped yet — no Week 9 cards to read
paragraphs: The board still shows the Week 8 board, generated November 2 at 12:08 p.m. UTC. There are no Week 9 cards yet, and the Monday prices above are now history, not live picks.

When the board flips, Thursday's cards will appear. If your book already has a Thursday line and you want a read on it now, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: No Week 9 cards yet — the board still shows Week 8, so run any Thursday price you hold through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle versus tickets
paragraphs: Two numbers get quoted about betting splits, and they are not the same thing. Tickets count how many bets were placed. Handle counts how much money was bet. A side can lead one and trail the other.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70 out of 100 tickets are on one team, but that team has only 40 percent of the handle. That means lots of smaller bets on that side, and fewer, bigger bets on the other side. It does not prove the bigger bets are smarter — but it tells you the crowd and the money are not saying the same thing.

That is why a split is only a starting point, never a pick on its own. When a real split does show the crowd and the money disagreeing, the useful question is what price you can get, and whether Check still says bet at that price.
items.takeaway: Tickets count bets, handle counts money — when they disagree, the crowd and the money are telling different stories, so check the price before acting.

items.headline: Board unchanged at the morning read — no new movement to report
paragraphs: At this morning's read, the board still shows the same Week 8 board as the evening read: Hit Rate on the Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings, and Balanced and Value both on Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings. The refresh to Week 9 has not landed.

Because the board has not refreshed, there is no new card movement to report. The last real movement on the Monday game was the November 2 morning board's: the Seattle moneyline getting pricier from -166 to -175, and Chicago +3 moving from FanDuel to DraftKings at the same -102. Those prices are now final results, not lines to chase.
If your book shows something different on Thursday's game, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you. Your book's price is the one that matters.
items.takeaway: No new card movement at the morning read — the board has not refreshed since the evening read, so the Week 8 cards are unchanged and now final.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The one thing worth waiting for this week is a real pending event: Baltimore's starting quarterback for Thursday. The starter decision is expected in the next day or two, and inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff. That is a genuine reason to let a Thursday price wait — a good number today can still be there, but a named starter can move it, so do not rush a Thursday bet before the quarterback is known.

When the board flips and Thursday's cards appear, run your book's price through Check before you bet. And one honest note: settlement is manual, so log the losers too. Monday's Hit Rate favorite lost — if you tracked it, it belongs in the record next to the +3 winner.
items.takeaway: Wait for Baltimore's quarterback news before rushing Thursday — then run your price through Check, and log Monday's loser with its winner.
